text: Your inbox overflows, a constant stream. You want to connect, but deep replies take effort. Too much to process, too little time for true thoughtfulness.
Then, a 'Like' or 'Got it!' button appears. A frictionless tap. Message acknowledged, conversation flows. It feels efficient, a perfect digital shortcut.
Soon, you're constantly tapping quick replies. You think it's just convenience, saving seconds. But why does that quick tap feel so satisfying, almost addictive?
It's intermittent reinforcement. Sometimes your tap gets a reaction, sometimes nothing. This unpredictable reward, plus low cognitive load, creates a powerful loop.
The cost is subtle: deeper communication erodes. You choose the easy button over meaningful interaction, making connections shallower. Trading depth for speed.
You'll still use quick replies, but now you understand their hidden pull. Choose when to tap for efficiency, and when to truly engage. You now see the system.
